title: US has used almost all of its long-range precision missiles including ATACMS and PrSM in Iran war: Report
content:
• The Iran war, which began on February 28, is in its sixth month and has led to the US using "virtually all" of its Army Tactical Missile Systems (ATACMS) and Precision Strike Missiles (PrSM).
• The US Patriot missile inventory significantly decreased from 2,330 before the war to between 759 and 827 by the end of July, with pre-war inventory levels for Patriots and THAADs not expected until 2029.
• Lockheed Martin manufactures ATACMS, PrSM, and THAAD missile systems, while Raytheon produces Tomahawk cruise missiles and Patriot interceptors.

title: US-Iran War LIVE: US closes in on Hormuz deal with Iran and Oman, eyes Wednesday announcement, Axios reports
content:
• A United States official confirmed that any temporary shipping routes through the Strait of Hormuz would not require permits, approvals, or fees.
• The prospect of a deal to normalise shipping in the Strait of Hormuz caused Brent crude to fall below $80 for the first time in more than three weeks.
• US Central Command (CENTCOM) stated that American forces have assisted more than 1,000 vessels in safely transiting the Strait of Hormuz over the past three months.

title: Iran seeks authority over inbound vessels as Hormuz reopening talks with Oman advance: Report
content:
• The Strait of Hormuz, a 34-km-wide waterway linking the Persian Gulf with the Indian Ocean, normally carries about one-fifth of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas shipments.
• Iran is negotiating with Oman for a temporary arrangement over the Strait of Hormuz, proposing Iranian control over inbound vessels, with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent expressing optimism for a deal.
• India's Shipping Minister Sarbananda Sonowal confirmed that the Indian-flagged vessel MSV Faize Noore Oliya, with 14 crew members (13 Indians), sank near Yemeni waters after being hit by a projectile.

title: No insurance, no fuel? Supreme Court seeks Centre's plan to stop fuel sales to uninsured vehicles
content:
• The Supreme Court directed IRDAI to increase the mandatory third-party insurance period for new private cars from three years to four years and for new two-wheelers from five years to six years.
• The Supreme Court noted that nearly 56% of vehicles on Indian roads do not have valid insurance, weakening the purpose of compulsory motor insurance under Section 146 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
• The Supreme Court directed the linking of Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) cameras with the Insurance Information Bureau database and the VAHAN portal to automatically issue e-challans to uninsured vehicles.

title: US nearly exhausted key long-range missile stockpiles after months of Iran war, report says
content:
• According to a recent CSIS report, the US utilized approximately 65% of its Patriot interceptor missiles and saw its THAAD ballistic missile interceptor inventories decrease by at least 38% between February and July during the conflict with Iran.
• The US has been involved in a five-month military campaign against Iran, launched in February, raising concerns about the depletion of key long-range missile stockpiles, including the Army Tactical Missile System (ATACMS) and the newer Precision Strike Missile (PrSM).
• Lockheed Martin is a manufacturer of critical missile systems such as ATACMS, PrSM, and THAAD, with each long-range missile costing over $1 million.

title: Government moves closer to restoring MDR on UPI merchant payments
content:
• FM Nirmala Sitharaman introduced a Bill in Lok Sabha proposing to remove a legal provision that currently bars banks and payment service providers from levying Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on specified electronic payment modes.
• The government had previously scrapped MDR on UPI transactions in January 2020 to encourage digital payments.
• The proposed amendments would empower the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to determine MDR on UPI transactions, potentially paving the way for charges on person-to-merchant (P2M) payments above ₹2,000.

title: India's private consumption projected to reach $1.9 trillion by 2030: FICCI-Deloitte report
content:
• India's private consumption is projected to reach $1.9 trillion by 2030, according to the FICCI-Deloitte report 'Consumer Trends: IGNITEing Growth and Governance'.
• For the first time, 'Improvement Notices' will be issued to manufacturers and retailers under the Legal Metrology Act, allowing them to rectify minor mistakes before case compounding, as stated by Nidhi Khare, Secretary, Department of Consumer Affairs.
• The Department of Consumer Affairs is working to introduce 'Smart Standards', with the aim of rolling them out on World Standards Day, October 14.

title: FISME seeks GST overhaul to ease MSME compliance
content:
• FISME has recommended protecting bona fide purchasers from Input Tax Credit (ITC) denial in cases of supplier defaults if they possess valid tax invoices, proof of receipt of goods/services, and have made payments via banking channels.
• FISME urged the government to introduce a 30-45 day timeline for GST refunds, along with automatic interest on delays and simplified procedures for accumulated ITC.
• To reduce compliance costs, FISME recommended faster implementation of the proposed 'One PAN-One Administration' framework, optional centralised compliance for businesses operating in multiple states, and uniform registration procedures.

title: Indian economy to hit USD 5-trillion mark in FY29 as per IMF: FM
content:
• The Indian economy is projected to cross the USD 5-trillion mark in FY29 (2028-29), with India's GDP at current prices estimated to be around USD 5.1 trillion by then, as per the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman.
• The Union Budget 2026-27 has announced several initiatives for the services sector, including the establishment of the National Institute of Hospitality and the creation of Regional Medical Hubs.
• The long-term vision for India is to achieve Viksit Bharat by 2047.
